page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.16-64 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration based on the Arm architecture. It is powered by Ampere Altra processors running at a sustained clock speed of 3.0 GHz. The instance is configured with 16 dedicated physical cores corresponding to 16 vCPUs, utilizing a single thread per core topology. Accompanying the compute capacity is 64.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio with 4.0 GB of RAM allocated per core.

Hardware accelerators are absent on this instance, with zero GPUs provisioned. Local storage is also omitted, meaning all non-volatile storage must be attached remotely via network block storage. Networking provisioning includes a complimentary public IPv4 address for external routing. Because each vCPU maps directly to an entire physical execution core rather than a simultaneous multithreading thread, compute execution avoids cross-thread resource contention.

The Arm64 architecture provides high compute density and energy efficiency, offering favorable cost efficiency for multi-threaded deployments compared to traditional x86 alternatives. Operating without integrated NVMe drives presents an architectural tradeoff that requires reliance on network volumes for persistent data. This instance profile fits scalable microservices, CI/CD build farms, web application hosting, and distributed container workloads designed for Arm64 runtimes.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.16-64 is an Arm-based general-purpose compute instance powered by Ampere Altra processors running at 3.0 GHz. The server provides 16 dedicated physical cores presenting 16 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading, paired with 64.0 GB of system memory to achieve a balanced 4.0 GB per core ratio. This configuration contains no local storage volumes and includes no GPU accelerators, relying on remote network storage for persistence while providing one complimentary public IPv4 address. The direct core allocation avoids hyper-threading contention, translating into reliable execution across parallel processing jobs. VM.Standard.A1.Flex.16-64 delivers cost-efficient compute capacity for multi-threaded web backends, software compilation pipelines, container infrastructure, and general enterprise workloads targeting the 64-bit Arm architecture.
